clusters.name: Cluster C (Anxious/Fearful)
items: Preoccupation with details, rules, lists, order, organization, or schedules (DSM p.771)
Perfectionism that interferes with task completion (DSM p.771)
Excessive devotion to work and productivity excluding leisure/friendships (DSM p.771)
Overconscientious, scrupulous, and inflexible about morality, ethics, or values (DSM p.771-772)
Inability to discard worn-out or worthless objects (DSM p.772)
Reluctance to delegate tasks or work with others (DSM p.772)
Miserly spending style toward self and others (DSM p.772)

criteria.thresholds: >=4/8 symptoms, early adulthood onset, pervasive across contexts (DSM p.771)
subtypes: Section III alternative model (Rigid Perfectionism + >=2 other traits: Perseveration, Intimacy avoidance, Restricted affectivity) (DSM p.888)

epidemiology.sex_ratio: 1:1 M:F in community samples (DSM p.774); 2:1 M:F in clinical samples (Synopsis ch.19)
epidemiology.heritability: High concordance in MZ vs DZ twins (Synopsis ch.19)
comorbidities: OCD (23%-32% of OCD patients have OCPD) (DSM p.271)
Major Depressive Disorder (DSM p.774; Synopsis ch.19)
epidemiology.prognosis: Chronic and stable course; can lead to depression in older age or herald schizophrenia in some adolescents (Synopsis ch.19)

etiology.genetic: Significantly higher concordance in MZ twins compared to DZ twins (Synopsis ch.19)
etiology.neurobiology: Impaired OFC cognitive flexibility; Ventral-to-Dorsal Striatum shift (compulsivity/habit loop) (StahlNeuro p.539, 575); DLPFC worry loop (StahlNeuro p.367)
etiology.environmental: Anal stage fixation (control and autonomy conflicts); over-controlling parental environment (Synopsis ch.19; Syllabus p.14, 26)

items: OCD: OCPD is ego-syntonic without intrusive obsessions/compulsions; OCD is ego-dystonic with intrusive obsessions and compulsions (DSM p.271, 774; Dulcan p.375)
Hoarding Disorder: OCPD hoarding lacks extreme living space clutter/fire hazard seen in Hoarding Disorder (DSM p.277, 774)
Narcissistic PD: Narcissists believe they achieved perfection; OCPD patients are self-critical and driven by rigid rules (DSM p.764, 775)
Schizoid PD: OCPD social detachment stems from work devotion/emotional discomfort; Schizoid lacks capacity/desire for intimacy (DSM p.775)
ASD: ASD repetitive behaviors provide apparent gratification; OCPD behaviors stem from rigid control/anxiety (Dulcan p.375)
key_numbers: 4 out of 8 criteria required for DSM-5-TR diagnosis (DSM p.771)
23%-32% rate of comorbid OCPD in patients diagnosed with OCD (DSM p.271)
Shortened REM latency and abnormal DST results in OCPD (Synopsis ch.19)

first_line: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) targeting perfectionism, black-and-white thinking, and work-life balance (Synopsis ch.19; Dulcan p.376)
Psychodynamic psychotherapy addressing isolation of affect and need for control (Synopsis ch.19)
second_line: Citalopram (SSRIs) — demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing rigidity and OCPD traits (Synopsis ch.19)
Sertraline / Fluoxetine / Fluvoxamine for comorbid OCD or depression (StahlKids p.208, 310, 452; Dulcan p.380)
Carbamazepine as adjunct for mood instability, rigidity, and hostility (Synopsis ch.19)
key_side_effects: SSRIs: Gastrointestinal distress, sexual dysfunction, activation/agitation in pediatric patients (StahlKids p.208, 310, 452)
Clomipramine: Sedation, anticholinergic effects, cardiac conduction delays / QTc prolongation (StahlKids p.133; Dulcan p.380)
treatment.monitoring: ECG/QTc and plasma concentration monitoring for Clomipramine (Dulcan p.380; Syllabus p.30); behavioral activation monitoring for pediatric SSRIs (StahlKids p.208)

high_yield: OCPD is ego-syntonic (views rigid standards as correct), whereas OCD is ego-dystonic (suffers from intrusive obsessions) (DSM p.265, 771; Dulcan p.375)
Requires >=4 of 8 criteria including perfectionism interfering with completion, reluctance to delegate, miserly spending, and rigidity (DSM p.771-772)
Hoarding in OCPD does not result in the extreme, room-blocking clutter seen in Hoarding Disorder (DSM p.774)
Neurobiology involves shift from Ventral Striatum reward loop to Dorsal Striatum habit/compulsivity loop and OFC cognitive inflexibility (StahlNeuro p.539, 575)
CBT targeting black-and-white thinking, perfectionism, and work-life balance is first-line psychotherapy (Synopsis ch.19)
In pediatric populations, evaluate Family Accommodation (FAS-IR) and involve parents in CBT (Dulcan p.367, 374)
